sections.title: Paper 1: Explorations in creative reading and writing

topics.title: Section A: Reading (one literature fiction text)

points.title: Question 1: identifying explicit information
content: Paper 1 Question 1: short form question, 4 marks.
AO1: identify and interpret explicit and implicit information and ideas.

points.title: Question 2: analysing language
content: Paper 1 Question 2: longer form question, 8 marks, on language in a printed extract.
AO2: explain, comment on and analyse how writers use language and structure to achieve effects and influence readers.

points.title: Question 3: analysing structure
content: Paper 1 Question 3: longer form question, 8 marks, on structure across the whole source.
AO2.

points.title: Question 4: critical evaluation
content: Paper 1 Question 4: extended question, 20 marks, critical evaluation of a statement about the source.
AO4: evaluate texts critically and support this with appropriate textual references.

points.title: Question 5: descriptive or narrative writing
content: Paper 1 Question 5: descriptive or narrative writing, 40 marks (24 for content and organisation, 16 for technical accuracy).
AO5: communicate clearly, effectively and imaginatively. AO6: use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures with accurate spelling and punctuation.

topics.title: Section A: Reading (two linked non-fiction texts)

points.title: Question 1: identifying true statements
content: Paper 2 Question 1: short form question, 4 marks, on true statements from the sources.
AO1.

points.title: Question 2: summarising differences or similarities
content: Paper 2 Question 2: longer form question, 8 marks, a summary of differences or similarities across both sources.
AO1: select and synthesise evidence from different texts.

points.title: Question 3: analysing language
content: Paper 2 Question 3: longer form question, 12 marks, on how a writer uses language.
AO2.

points.title: Question 4: comparing writers' viewpoints and methods
content: Paper 2 Question 4: extended question, 16 marks, comparing writers' ideas and perspectives and how they are conveyed.
AO3: compare writers' ideas and perspectives, as well as how these are conveyed, across two or more texts.

points.title: Question 5: writing to present a viewpoint
content: Paper 2 Question 5: writing to present a viewpoint, 40 marks (24 for content and organisation, 16 for technical accuracy).
AO5 and AO6.

official_source.title: AQA GCSE English Language 8700 specification
official_source.note: First assessment June 2017. Two written papers of 80 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes each; spoken language is a separately reported non-exam endorsement.

approach: Official AQA assessment structure. English Language has no topic content: leaves are the question types of each paper. No textbook organisation has been supplied.
notes: Leaf ids are unchanged from the earlier tree. Paper 1 Question 1 in the 2026 sample is four 1-mark multiple choice parts that still assess AO1 (A.1).
